proposed_from.topic: Canonical active-face certificates for exact-hit saturation-policy design. This is a new attempt at parent exp_saturation_exacthit_deficiency_design, not a retry of its nonmeasurable full-open-simplex scaffold. Fix K>=3, cluster size n0, distinct rational interior counts m_k, unrestricted binary within-cluster potential-outcome schedules, and exact-slice welfare U_k. Compare exact-count allocation a with nominal-label Bernoulli assignment p, whose exact-hit rates are q=Bp with B_kl=Pr{Bin(n0,m_l/n0)=m_k}. For each active face define the all-Borel randomized-selector Gaussian simple-regret value G_A(v,r), with singleton value zero and infinity at action-relevant zero information. Construct a terminating rational certificate that analytically prunes the exact-count boundary, partitions only closed positive-rate and covariance cells, returns outward epsilon brackets and all-minimizer cells for inf_a G_K(v,a) and inf_p G_K(v,Bp), and chooses lexicographically first designs only on an explicit finite certified grid. Realize every finite selector by a fixed inverse-CDF map jointly Borel in pilot covariance, screening and decision statistics, and an auxiliary uniform; covariance partitions apply only when |A|>=2. For primitive transfer, work at attainable binary full-tie baselines with v in a declared positive domain and O(C^-1/2) covariance neighborhoods, not exact membership in arbitrary singleton variance boxes. Prove a uniform calibrated three-way-split LAN risk sandwich over deterministic allocation sequences, including a vanishing-share converse and partial-tie subfaces. Return certified regret and cluster-count ratios; decide strict loss from the rational total-hit condition and provide finite certificates for positive excess over the mass floor, without claiming a total numerical equality oracle. Use the n0=6 menu m=(1,2,4), legal variance box [1/8,1/4]^3, and Egger et al.'s Kenya saturation design as the worked consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolver derived G_K(v,a)>=kappa sqrt(v_i/a_i), giving the explicit uniform prune eta=1/1024 on [1/8,1/4]^3, and realized every variance there at a full tie using W in {0,1/2,1}. Ordered finite cells plus inverse-CDF weights give a canonical Borel evaluator. A vanishing allocation share makes local alternatives indistinguishable and forces divergent scaled regret. For the three-label menu on active face {1,2}, exact rational interval arithmetic gives p3*=0, p1*=0.289596897074... and regret ratio in [1.296043143254,1.296043143255]. Destructive checks rejected the parent's illegal [1,2]^3 binary witness, exact covariance membership in arbitrary V, global least-rational choices, and a purported total equality decision; the corrected statements preserve the model and target. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the quantitatively uniform primitive risk sandwich for the finite canonical receipt family, combining calibrated ratio errors, screening tails, enlarged covariance cells, finite-prior uniform LAN, and one computable diagonal schedule. EARLY KILL TEST: Build a fixed-tolerance n0=6,K=3 receipt on [1/8,1/4]^3 with eta=1/1024, exact singleton branches, boundary-safe inverse-CDF decoding, a full-observation finite-prior lower bound, and independent-screen upper risk; reproduce the solved active-pair interval and one full-tie three-arm covariance before attempting the general theorem. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The kernel is a covariance-set robust saturation design. Gao, Ge, and Qian characterize generic multi-marginal partial-identification problems, while Aronow, Green, and Lee obtain sharp two-potential-outcome variance bounds. Neither paper incorporates the within-slice averaging map generated by one unrestricted interference schedule, the exact-hit matrix, or experimental allocation choice. Harshaw, Middleton, and Sävje optimize conservative quadratic upper bounds for fixed designs and estimators; the explicit comonotone--countermonotone construction proves that no single covariance envelope represents the full compatible image sharply in every direction. Jiang, Imai, and Malani and Baird, Bohren, McIntosh, and Özler analyze two-stage saturation inference and power while fixing the design and using conservative or imposed covariance information. The advance is the sharp joint covariance image for all assignment-cell couplings together with an exact convex design criterion whose optimality is certified by multi-marginal linear-program duals and finite KKT witnesses. The construction retains the finite-population correction \(-\Xi\), so it assumes neither a diagonal covariance nor thinning homogeneity.

seed_details.anchor: Joo2025, Introduction, Theorems 2.1--2.3, Proposition 3.2, Theorem 4.2, Section 5.1, and Concluding Remarks
seed_details.anchor_read: The proof obtains a least-favorable prior and a unique Bayes rule on a compact mean cube, then proves covariance continuity by subsequence compactness and density convergence; the numerical section maximizes the Bayes risk directly and reports decision boundaries.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace arbitrary numerical maximization on one covariance matrix by directed lower Bayes integration and represented-rule upper bounds on ordered rational covariance and allocation cells, after analytically pruning zero-information boundaries.
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches for rational certification of Gaussian minimax regret, covariance-cell minimax receipts, and exact-hit saturation regret found Joo2025 and GuggenbergerHuang2025 but no finite continuum certificate or all-minimizer enclosure.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Joo2025 because the unique least-favorable-prior rule is already computationally tractable.
seed_details.rebuttal: The source proves a characterization and continuity and performs floating-point optimization on fixed compact instances; it does not certify noncompact contrast tails, continuous design cells, singleton faces, or every outer minimizer.

seed_details.anchor_read: The central construction slices a locally asymptotically normal experiment into Gaussian subproblems, proves a local asymptotic minimax lower bound, and attains it with efficient-statistic treatment rules; its smooth fixed experiment does not include pilot-indexed finite receipts or allocation boundaries.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace pointwise limit-experiment transfer by one quantitative comparison for calibrated ratio errors, finite polyhedral selector events, screening tails, enlarged covariance cells, and finite-prior likelihood ratios, uniform over deterministic allocations and tie faces.
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches pairing randomization-based two-stage central limit theory with minimax selector risk found LiuHudgens2014 and JiangImaiMalani2023 for fixed estimators and Joo2025 for assumed locally uniform normality, but no design-uniform receipt risk sandwich.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Hirano--Porter plus a finite-population central limit theorem and Slutsky's lemma.
seed_details.rebuttal: Slutsky does not control expected regret for a pilot-selected discontinuous selector family, covariance-cell boundaries, unbounded local gaps, or allocation sequences with vanishing action information.

proposed_from.literature_map: The Gaussian-decision thread begins with Hirano and Porter, whose limit-experiment construction yields local asymptotic minimax treatment rules in smooth models. Joo's Theorems 2.1--2.3 characterize the many-arm minimax-regret Bayes rule, Proposition 3.2 establishes covariance continuity, and Theorem 4.2 transfers a covariance plug-in rule under an assumed locally uniform central limit theorem. Guggenberger and Huang instead discretize nature, alternate finite-game best responses, and prove convergence of numerical lower and upper bounds. None returns a finite rational cover of continuous allocation and covariance domains, a Borel pilot decoder, or every minimizer cell. The assignment-based thread starts with Hudgens and Halloran's partial-interference potential outcomes. VanderWeele and Tchetgen Tchetgen distinguish fixed-count type-A from independent-Bernoulli type-B assignment, which supplies the conditioning identity behind \(q=Bp\). Liu and Hudgens derive large-sample randomization inference for two-stage designs, and Jiang, Imai, and Malani give unbiased estimators, conservative variances, tests, and power formulas for multiple assignment mechanisms while fixing their distribution. Baird and coauthors choose saturation distributions for power under an imposed covariance model. Those results do not optimize all-selector welfare regret or compare exact hits. Aronow, Green, and Lee's sharp two-margin coupling and Li and Ding's vector finite-population central limit theory are the nearest covariance and approximation tools. Han, Owusu, and Shin study pairwise empirical-success ranking and optimize a nonasymptotic regret bound, not the exact-hit all-selector game. Lu, Shi, and Ding address cross-cluster spillovers and show why the Kenya consumer must be a prospective isolated-cluster replication. The surviving intersection is therefore a certified optimal design problem: a rational active-face receipt, a uniform assignment-based risk bridge, and an exact algebraic equality frontier for Bernoulli-label information loss.
